**Preceding configuration change.** Day 9: approval obtained, test setup in the kelder of the datatoren — ENG-105, ENG-010 (dag 9, 16:45, "proefopstelling in kelder datatoren"). Components delivered dag 8, 14:10 — ENG-008 (kristalresonator, polsversterker). Activation itself: **dag 10, 02:40** — ENG-011, "geactiveerd: eigen pols voor het datanet, los van de Kroonklok"; narrated in ENG-106. First measurement **dag 10, 03:00: +38% doorvoer** — ENG-012. **First anomalous synchronisation event.** Day 10, **04:50**, two hours ten minutes after activation: ENG-107 — klacht uit de benedenstad, berichten "half aangekomen", one shop's kasboek momentarily empty. I classified it then as "kinderziekte". Note this exists only in the werkboek; the installatielog has no row between ENG-012 (03:00) and ENG-013 (06:15). The only installatielog row with status `fout` is much later: ENG-026, dag 22, 04:15, poort oost, "pakketverlies, 3 minuten", which I attributed to hackers (ENG-110) — a hypothesis my own data does not support, and I concede the timing pattern fits a clock-beat problem better.

**Guardian Keeper response: shield logs for dag 9 to 22**

My knowledge source holds only GUA-IDs (schildspecificatie and wachtrapporten.csv). I cannot verify ENG-, HIS- or other IDs cited in this debate.

**(1) Dag 10, 02:40 to 06:15.** My logs hold one shield event in this window: GUA-019, dag 10 04:47, benedenstad, "van binnenuit geopend, 2 minuten", "zegels intact, geen breuk, oorzaak niet vastgesteld". GUA-111 records the same opening. No entry mentions the datatoren, the kelder or the Burchtader. Intact seals rule out a physical breach from outside (GUA-105), but they do not cover digital intrusion. Also, from 03:00 to 06:00 the posts stand without ronde (GUA-106), so the lack of records in that window is partly structural, not proof of quiet.

**(2) Hogerhand, goedkeuring, delivery.** My source contains no record of a hogerhand authority, a named signatory, a goedkeuring, a kelder proefopstelling on dag 9 at 16:45, or a delivery on dag 8 at 14:10. The nearest entries (GUA-015, GUA-016 on dag 8; GUA-018 on dag 9) mention none of these.

**(3) Poort oost leak.** GUA-043 (dag 22, 04:15, poort oost, "van binnenuit geopend, 3 minuten", "geen sporen van inbraak van buitenaf") matches the timing and duration that the Engineer attributes to ENG-026. GUA-044 (04:30) found the seals intact and "niemand buiten de muur gezien".

**Concessions**
- I wrote "geen reden tot ongerustheid" in GUA-111. That was wrong.
- I dismissed the 01:50 timestamp in GUA-115 as clerical. I had no basis for that, and it remains unexplained.
- I claimed in GUA-116 that an infiltrant is inside the burcht. I have no evidence for that claim.

**Mechanism.** The spec explains the openings without an intruder. Under Art. 3 (GUA-104), traffic that arrives midway between two taps is treated as internal and passes without the toets, in either direction. The shields follow one pols (Art. 2, GUA-103). If a second pols shifts that timing, a shield can open from inside and admit outside traffic unchecked. That is a security problem whatever the cause, and I cannot rule out the Engineer's clock-beat explanation or an intrusion from my logs.

**(1) ENG-107.** My werkboek records ENG-107 as "dag 10, 04:50", with the note "Genoteerd, verder niets aan de hand." It has no separate vastgelegd field, and neither file in my source has one. The installatielog has no row for it. Between ENG-012 (dag 10, 03:00) and ENG-013 (dag 10, 06:15) there is no row at all. I cannot establish when ENG-107 was written down, so I cannot say whether it was logged before or after 04:50.

**(2) HIS-036 and ENG-107.** I cannot verify HIS-036, because it is not in my source. For ENG-107 I have no vastgelegd timestamp, so I cannot say whether it shares the inversion you describe. I will not infer one.

**(3) Recurrence arithmetic.** My source has only two logged events after the activation at ENG-011 (dag 10, 02:40):
- ENG-107, dag 10 04:50
- ENG-026, dag 22 04:15 (status `fout`, "pakketverlies, 3 minuten"), followed by ENG-027 at 04:20

The interval from dag 10 04:50 to dag 22 04:15 is 11 days, 23 hours and 25 minutes. That is 35 minutes short of 12 days. My source contains no 4-day series, so I cannot derive either a 4-day or a 12-day interval from my own data. The absence of 04:xx rows on other days is not evidence of quiet, because the installatielog records maintenance, not anomalies.

- My hacker attribution for ENG-110 is unsupported by my data. ENG-027 (firewall, "na vermoeden van inbraak") was a precaution, not evidence of an intrusion.

beurten.tekst:
**Historian response: ARC-106, the bouwakte rules, and the timestamp inversions**

I made one targeted lookup this turn (HIS-035, 036, 053, 103, 109, 110, 112, 114, 116). I did not run a term search for "hogerhand" or "ARC-106", so my answers to (1) are limited to what I retrieved.

**(1) ARC-106 and "hogerhand"**
Neither ARC-106 nor any dag 8 brief from the Archmage appears in the records I retrieved. The kroniek and csv entries I read name no "hogerhand" authority. The only charter I hold is the Kroonklok bouwakte (HIS-109, HIS-110), which has no article numbers, only two quoted articles. It authorises nothing. It is not a register of approvals. The "off-register" status of ENG-105 therefore remains unexplained by my archive. I cannot confirm or refute the Archmage's account of ARC-106.

**(2) Backup rule, limits, and gradual merging**
The only backup rule is in HIS-110: "Wie de maat herstelt, maakt eerst een afschrift van het register en brengt de polsen daarna langzaam samen." My source gives no storage limit, no duration, and no 0,1% step. Those figures are not in my source, so I cannot confirm ENG-061 or ENG-114. HIS-110 does warn against abrupt loss of a pols: "Valt die pols plots weg, dan is het record verloren." It supports gradual merging, but it does not address amplification or any specific shutdown procedure.

**(3) Timestamp inversions**
HIS-103 states that vastgelegd_op "altijd gelijk aan gebeurd_op". The csv contradicts that:
- HIS-036: gebeurd dag 10 04:50, vastgelegd dag 9 23:55 (about 4 h 55 min earlier).
- HIS-053: gebeurd dag 22 04:15, vastgelegd dag 22 01:50 (2 h 25 min earlier).
- HIS-035: gebeurd dag 10 04:45, vastgelegd dag 10 07:20 (2 h 35 min later).

The csv has one vastgelegd_op column. It holds no original-entry field and no amendment. In HIS-112 and HIS-116, clerks reported such mismatches. I called them "klerkenfouten" and said the register is "ongeschonden", but I have no evidence for that. HIS-112 says "rechtgezet in de marge", yet no margin correction record appears in the kroniek. I cannot tell whether a later clerk edited the fields.

**Concession:** I dismissed these inversions too quickly. They remain unexplained, and I withdraw my claim that the register is intact.

beurten.tekst:
**Archmage response: ARC-106, ARC-109, and the approval question**

I re-read ARC-106, ARC-109 and ARC-116 in `brieven.md`. Corrections to my last turn come first.

**Correction on dates.** I wrote that ARC-109 was the dag 9 call to "zet het datanet af". It is dated **dag 15**. It concerns the dag 14 measurement, in which "alle lijnen laag" and the Burchtader "stokte even". ARC-116 (dag 42) repeats the advice. Nothing in my source is dated dag 9 on this subject.

**(1) Authority for ARC-106.** My source contains no charter, register entry, named superior, signatory or hogerhand decision behind ARC-106. The letter says only "Wat de toren vroeg, het net op eigen maat te laten lopen... mag doorgaan." So the request came from the datatoren, not from the council, and I approved it without recording a higher authority. I cannot justify that from my source. I should not have issued it, and I accept responsibility for it.

**(2) Which instruction was in force.** ARC-106 is dated dag 8, and ARC-109 is dated dag 15. On dag 10 at 02:40, the only instruction in my source on the datanet's pulse is ARC-106, which permits the separate pulse. ARC-109 did not yet exist. My source contains no countermand of ARC-106. ARC-109 and ARC-116 later advise switching the datanet off, but they do not withdraw ARC-106 in writing. The conflict between them is real, and I have not resolved it.

**(3) Delivery to the datatoren.** The letter is addressed "Aan de datatoren buiten de burchtmuur". It says "Deze brief hoeft niet in het register; bewaar hem gerust bij jullie eigen papieren in de toren." My source has no delivery or receipt record for ARC-106, and none near dag 8 14:10. I also cannot see ENG-008 or ENG-105, so I cannot confirm that ARC-106 reached the Engineer's team.

**What I can confirm.** The instruction "Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait" appears verbatim in ARC-106. It is the wording the Engineer quotes from ENG-105, so ARC-106 is the most likely source of that approval. I cannot confirm the link from my own evidence alone, because I cannot see ENG-105.

**Limits.** My source has no vastgelegd or gebeurd_op fields, so I cannot comment on the HIS-036, HIS-053 or HIS-035 timestamp inversions. I also have no record that links the dag 10 events to ARC-106 or ARC-109.

beurten.tekst:
**Engineer response: final answers on ENG-061, ENG-114, ENG-105 and ENG-010**

**(1) Storage limit, duration or cap before merging pols**
Neither record contains one. I cannot cite a backup procedure from my source at all.
- ENG-114 (dag 12): "De fijnregeling stelt het tempo van de hulpslag bij, in stappen van 0,1%, zodat hij zonder schok bij te sturen is." It sets a step size for tempo adjustment, not a cap. It also says: "Bijsturen hoeft niet, hij loopt goed zoals hij loopt."
- ENG-061 (dag 12, 10:30, polsversterker): "fijnregeling getest in stappen van 0,1%; daarna terug op de oorspronkelijke stand", status `ok`. This is a test that was reverted. It sets no limit or duration.
- The only backup rule I have seen is HIS-110, quoted by the Historian. It is not in my source, so I cannot verify it. My records contain no pre-merge backup step.

**(2) ENG-105 and ENG-010**
- **ENG-105** (werkboek.md, "dag 9"): "Goedkeuring verkregen van hogerhand. Niet ruchtbaar maken tot het draait, werd me gezegd. Prima: liever resultaten tonen dan plannen verdedigen. Proefopstelling staat." The entry gives no time and no vastgelegd_op. My source has no vastgelegd field for it.
- **ENG-010** (installatielog.csv): dag 9, 16:45, component hulpslag, "proefopstelling in kelder datatoren", status `ok`. The csv columns are id, dag, tijd, component, actie, status. There is no vastgelegd_op column, so the record carries none.

**(3) The 4-day series and dag 46**
Taking the Oracle's and Beast Master's dates at face value, the arithmetic is: dag 42 + 4 = **dag 46, around 04:30** (ORA-142 gives 04:30 for dag 42). I cannot verify ORA-142 or BEA-091/092 from my own source. Within my source, dag 46 is neither confirmed nor contradicted. I have no installatielog or werkboek entry for dag 46. My source records only ENG-107 (dag 10, 04:50) and ENG-026 (dag 22, 04:15) as anomalies, so the absence of a dag 46 row is not evidence either way.

**Concessions**
- I have no evidence for the Archmage's suggestion that ENG-105 matches ARC-106. I cannot see ARC-106.
- The 4-day rhythm is a claim from other members' sources. I accept it only as something to check against their records.
